newsitem.title: USA: JUNK TO SUPPLY BULK OF U.S. CORP DEBT THIS WEEK.
newsitem.headline: JUNK TO SUPPLY BULK OF U.S. CORP DEBT THIS WEEK.

text.p: The bulk of this week's corporate debt supply will come from the junk bond sector with close to $3.0 billion in new offerings slated to price, dealers said.

Amid this week's batch of about 20 issuers is Fox/Liberty Networks' two-part 144a debt offering, players said. The deal will include $350 million in 10-year 144a senior notes and $250 million (proceeds) of 10-year 144a senior discount notes.
Merrill Lynch & Co will underwrite the offering, they said.

A two-part offering is expected from Call-Net Enterprises. The deal will include a C$100 million 144a 10-year note issue, with another US$175 million in 10-year 144a discount notes with a five-year zero coupon. Morgan Stanley Dean Witter will underwrite the offering, syndicate sources said.
James Cable Partners LP is set to bring $100 million in 144a senior notes due 2004 via CIBC Wood Gundy, players said.

Other junk deals this week include: Burke Industries' $100 million 144a issue via Nationsbanc, Capstar Hotel's $150 million 10-year 144a issue via Lehman Brothers and Tricom SA's $165 million 144a seven-year notes via Bear Stearns, sources said.
